description:
A finalizer that runs once every field has finished: it pools the per-field summaries into the campaign summary, verifies the dataset is complete and internally consistent, and writes the checksum file covering the raw data set.

## Background

Field executions run independently and each writes only its own paths, so nothing in the dataset pools across fields while they are running — that is what lets them run concurrently without a shared writer. The pooled campaign summary and the checksum file are therefore campaign-scoped artefacts with exactly one writer, and this is it.

The checksum boundary matters as much as the checksums. The raw data set — root manifest, shard records, field summaries, and the pooled summary — is what a reader must be able to verify. Derived artefacts such as the analysis report, generated figures, and model-comparison outputs quote those numbers and sometimes quote the checksums themselves, so including them would make the checksum file depend on documents that depend on it. Keeping the boundary explicit avoids that cycle and makes "verify the data I was given" a well-defined operation.

Finalization is also the campaign's completeness check. A dataset whose cells are partly completed, partly halted and partly missing is not a finished campaign, and the difference between a halted cell and an absent one is the difference between a recorded falsification and a gap.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The finalizer pools every field summary into one campaign `summary.csv` carrying, per $(q,n)$, the pooled permanent and determinant counts and terminal state. Completed rows carry point estimates with intervals and applicable acceptance verdicts; halted rows carry their reason and leave every final estimate and verdict empty.
- [hard] REQ-02: Finalization is deterministic: running it twice on one dataset produces byte-identical outputs, and the pooled result does not depend on the order fields finished or the order files are read.
- [hard] REQ-03: The finalizer refuses to finalize a dataset in which a cell named by the frozen manifest has no terminal record, naming every such cell.
- [hard] REQ-04: The finalizer verifies that per-shard records agree with the field summaries that pooled them, and refuses on any disagreement rather than overwriting either.
- [hard] REQ-05: `checksums.sha256` covers exactly the raw data set — root manifest, shard records, field summaries, and the pooled summary — and covers no derived artefact.
- [hard] REQ-06: A verification path re-checks a finalized dataset against its checksum file and reports pass or the failing paths.
- [hard] REQ-07: The finalizer writes only campaign-scoped paths and modifies no field-scoped file, so finalizing cannot alter the data it summarises.
- [hard] REQ-08: Outputs carry data and mechanical provenance only, with no interpretive statement about what the pooled numbers mean.

## Notes

A campaign that halted under its predeclared rule finalizes normally: the halt is a recorded terminal state, and the resulting dataset is a complete record of a falsified run rather than an incomplete one.
title: Deterministic finalization of a completed campaign dataset
